items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: AGVA president was there, Mr. Joey Adams, you know.

ctx.x: 1960. I was being reintroduced by the father of rhythm, I call him the jeweler of the pages. John W. Bubbles. He's number one 'Sporting Life' for Porgy and Bess. And he sang, he told the ladies and gentlemen of the audience he said, that I was back. Chuck and Chuckles. You see, and he was -- he was involved in some kind of a tuition at the time, because these publishers of Amsterdam News and Jet Magazine, Johnson Publications, you see, Ebony, and I think they had another world going too, and in those days and 60…

you see? Oh, you had some of the best there is in the world, you see, and the show they only had -- they had a time limit, they was limited to about three hours, I think, something like that, till midnight. And, I -- well see he died, he was -- he was a favorite, John W. Bubbles. See. And he -- he sang 'Lady Be Good' and told the ladies and the gentlemen, he was going to sing 'Lady Be Good' and then that Chuck Green was coming out of Chuckie and Chuckles, and dance.
